## Economy

### Currency  -  Fragments of the Primordial

All precious metals  -  gold, silver, copper, and platinum  -  as well as gemstones, are **fragments of B's physical remains** from the Great Sacrifice. This is why these materials are rare, valuable, and inherently magical (many spells require costly components). **Nobody knows this.** It is one of the deepest cosmological secrets of the setting, and its revelation is intended to be a major campaign-defining moment.

The standard currency system follows familiar denominations:
- **Copper Pieces (cp)**  -  everyday transactions
- **Silver Pieces (sp)**  -  standard wage and trade currency
- **Gold Pieces (gp)**  -  high-value trade, magic items, large transactions
- **Platinum Pieces (pp)**  -  extremely rare, used by major guilds and high-level commerce

### The Mint  -  Northeast Settlement Cluster (Name TBD)

Currency is minted in a cluster of settlements in the **northeast** of the continent. This area consists of **one major settlement and three minor ones**, plus two smaller nearby settlements that assist in exporting the currency. This was the site of the royal mint before the monster invasion, and after the reconquering, production resumed here. It remains the **backbone of the continental economy**.

This region also contains the **greatest known mines** for both precious metals and gemstones, making it the single most economically vital area in the recovered territories. *(Further detail on the northeast settlement cluster to be defined when locations are developed.)*

---

## Major Industries

### Mining & Prospecting

The **northeast settlement cluster** is the heart of mining operations, producing the bulk of precious metals and gemstones that fuel the economy. Additional mines exist in the recovered south and east. Operations are managed by the Miners' & Prospectors' Guild with strict quotas and safety regulations.

### Metalworking & Smithing

**Emberforge** is the industrial heart of the mortal races. Its volcanic forges produce:
- Weapons and armor for the Last Stand military
- Tools for farming, construction, and mining
- Components for arcane research and enchantment
- Unique alloys made possible by volcanic heat and rare ores

Emberforge's technology is the most advanced on the continent, and its weapons are considered the finest available.

### Agriculture & The Fertile Forests

The forests surrounding the three capitals  -  where the Last Stand was founded  -  are exceptionally nutrient-rich, producing abundant food. This fertility is not natural: below Skywatch and Weaveheart, extending to the side of Emberforge, lies a **massive cave of arcane-reactive crystals** that blankets the entire area where the forest grows on top. The crystals' ambient energy seeps into the soil, supercharging its productivity. *(This is a plot hook to be developed.)*

Staple crops across the recovered territories include:
- Grains (wheat, barley, oats) in the temperate regions
- Rice, exotic fruits, and spices in the subtropical south
- Livestock (cattle, sheep, poultry) across both regions

Food security is a strategic priority  -  the granaries of the three capitals maintain enough reserves to survive a siege of several years.

### Arcane Industry & The Thormvuld Family

The **Thormvuld** family  -  dwarven arcane engineers established in a one-shot before the campaign  -  are the most prominent and proficient magical item producers on the continent. They originate from the **northeast settlement cluster** and also own a **small settlement south of it**, dedicated to their workshops and foundries.

**Weaveheart** also produces high-quality enchanted equipment and houses a prestigious **mage college** that trains new spellcasters and advances arcane research. However, the Thormvulds remain the premier producers of magical goods.

### Monster Hunting Industry

The continent-wide adventurers' guild (Drakh Ix'thar) is the primary controller of this industry. Settlements, caravans, and military outposts contract the guild to clear monster nests, eliminate threats, and reclaim dangerous sites. This is one of the largest economic sectors, as the reconquering effort relies on it for frontier expansion.

### The Last Alliance Military

The unified army of the three capitals functions as a major economic force in its own right. Beyond its direct military role, it contracts local mercenary companies for specific operations  -  reconquering a settlement, securing a resource outpost, or reinforcing a frontier position. These contracts inject significant coin into local economies.

### Sea Trade & Ports

A major settlement to the **southeast**  -  heavily fortified, coastal, and highly defensible  -  serves as one of the main sea trade hubs. Another port settlement to the **east** provides additional sea connections. Together, they form the backbone of maritime commerce.

Major exports include:
- From the south: exotic fruits, spices, timber, rare herbs
- From the northeast: precious metals, gemstones, minted currency
- From Emberforge: weapons, armor, industrial goods
- From Weaveheart: enchanted items, magical components

---

## Trade Routes

### The Eastern Sea Route

A series of ports along the eastern coast, connecting the southern ports to the heartlands. Ships carry goods north and south, stopping at waypoint towns. Safer than land travel and handles the bulk of bulk trade.

### Crassian's Dust Circle

An overland trade circuit connecting all major settlements  -  the three capitals, the northeast settlement cluster, the southeastern port, and the eastern port. The circuit was named after the great cloud of dust that arose when it was completed, as large trade caravans from across the recovered territories began using it all at once, covering the land and skies for days.

### The Frontier Road

A dangerous, partially reclaimed road extending west from the heartlands into contested territory. Used by military supply convoys and frontier settlers, always under heavy guard.

## Economic Challenges

- **Resource scarcity**  -  many mines and forests in the north and west remain under monster control, limiting access to certain resources
- **Trade disruption**  -  monster attacks on caravans and ships, while reduced, still occur
- **War economy inflation**  -  military production consumes resources that could otherwise go to civilian development
- **Black market**  -  a thriving underground trade in monster parts, illegal magical components, and contraband operates in the shadows, often connected to existing organizations
